title: [Mouse Without Borders] v0.101.2652.0: Settings rejects MWB with "Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature" because Settings.exe and MWB binaries are signed with different certificates

judgment.rationale: The SettingsSync rejection is directly explained by the implemented policy and was reconfirmed on 0.102.3001.0 with the same two Microsoft signer certificates assigned to opposite executables. Correct release signer consistency without weakening peer verification.
evidence: The original 0.101.2652.0 report records repeated `untrusted-signature` exceptions in both service modes and different valid signer thumbprints for Settings and MWB binaries.

The October 27 comment confirms the same exception on 0.102.3001.0 and same certificate pair reversed across the executables; key/settings resets and service-mode changes failed, while downgrade to 0.101.2362.0 restored pairing.

At upstream main 9227a8497750, MeetsSigningPolicy requires HaveSameTrustedMicrosoftSigner for embedded-signed peers; HaveMatchingSignerCertificate compares signer RawData with FixedTimeEquals. This accounts for the rejection: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/Utilities/NamedPipePeerVerification.cs#L265-L334
The issue links #50480, #49949, and #50615. Issue #51620 repeats the exact 0.102.3001.0 mismatch and is duplicate coverage, not a second fix candidate.
judgment.recommended_action: Route a narrowly scoped release signer-consistency correction while preserving the peer-signature trust check

fix_assessment.rationale: The certificate mismatch and rejection condition are demonstrated. Align release signing with the existing peer policy; the evidence does not justify broadening trust to a subject-name-only comparison.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Settings and MWB peers on a signer accepted by the existing policy
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The shipped Settings and MWB binaries are Microsoft-signed with different leaf certificates, while SettingsSync requires the trusted peer signer certificates to match exactly.
plan: Trace release signing assignment for the affected Settings and MWB binaries and align the released peer binaries with the existing accepted-signer policy.
Retain rejection of untrusted peers; do not replace trusted-signer validation with a broad publisher-name comparison solely to accommodate the release mismatch.
verification: For each affected package, verify both signatures and the existing signer comparison in both service modes; confirm New key and SettingsSync succeed without the rejection.

confidence.rationale: The exact comparison and affected-release signer identities directly account for the rejection; only the specific signing-pipeline correction remains to be chosen.

issue_context.summary: SettingsSync rejects MWB because valid Settings and MWB release executables have different Microsoft signer certificates.
known_information: On 0.101.2652.0, repeated `untrusted-signature` errors, different Settings/MWB signer thumbprints, and failure in both service modes are documented.
On 0.102.3001.0, the same error and certificate pair were confirmed with the certificates assigned to opposite executables.
Downgrading both devices to 0.101.2362.0 restored pairing for the commenter.
inferences: The release signing assignment is the likely correction point; the specific pipeline change remains to be determined.
issue_context.analysis: The report provides the precise exception and signer data; current source confirms exact equality of trusted leaf certificates. Preserve that boundary and correct release signer consistency. #51620 repeats the same failure and is not an independent fix candidate.
initial_investigation: Inspected NamedPipePeerVerification.cs at upstream main 9227a8497750: MeetsSigningPolicy delegates to HaveSameTrustedMicrosoftSigner, and the final comparison uses FixedTimeEquals on signer RawData: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/Utilities/NamedPipePeerVerification.cs#L265-L334
Refreshed the complete body, two comments, links, labels, and timestamp; no upload attachment is present.
Compared #51620: its commenter repeats the same exception and certificates on 0.102.3001.0, making #50795 the primary tracking issue.

actions.label: Route signer-consistency correction
actions.note: Lightweight direction only; preserve the trusted-peer boundary and select release-signing details in the owning work item.
